report.title: Checkout slowdown consistent with DB connection pool contention
report.summary: During 14:15–14:30 UTC, checkout latency and API error rate increased while request volume stayed steady. Sampled traces concentrate delay in inventory.reserve, dominated by waiting to acquire a DB connection. A checkout release shortly before the spike reduced the inventory client pool max, consistent with the observed contention.

findings.text: Checkout-api p95 rose to 2840ms (from 420ms baseline) and API error rate rose to 6.8% while traffic stayed ~120 rps during 14:15–14:30 UTC.
Representative slow trace shows inventory.reserve consuming 2520ms, with 2190ms in db.pool.acquire; payments.authorize is ~130ms and the SELECT itself ~180ms.
Across sampled slow traces, 18/20 include db pool waits above 1800ms; this supports pool contention but does not prove all requests behave this way.

Dependency metrics show payment authorization p95 stayed near baseline and DB CPU stayed near baseline; pool pending requests increased from 0 to 84, consistent with connection contention rather than CPU saturation.

nextSteps: Pull time-aligned metrics from inventory-api and inventory-db for connection acquire wait, active/idle connections, and pool pending to confirm the contention is present across the fleet, not only in sampled traces.

report.uncertainty: The evidence strongly indicates connection-acquire waiting, but the traces are sampled and don’t establish population-wide behavior. report.customerUpdate: Between 14:15–14:30 UTC we observed slower checkout responses and elevated API errors. proposal.action: Revert checkout-api inventory client connection pool max from 5 back to 20.
proposal.rationale: Checkout p95 latency and error rate increased in the incident window, and sampled slow traces show most time spent waiting on db.pool.acquire within inventory.reserve. A recent checkout release reduced the pool max from 20 to 5, consistent with the observed pool pending increase and long pool waits.
proposal.expectedEffect: Reduce connection-acquire wait time in inventory.reserve, lowering checkout p95 latency and reducing timeouts/errors if they are driven by pool contention.

report.title: INC-0244: focus on inventory-to-db connectivity
report.summary: Checkout latency and error rate rose at 17:14 UTC while request rate stayed steady. Slow traces concentrate time in inventory’s database TCP connect/handshake. Network telemetry shows elevated rejected connections on the inventory-to-db path after a firewall policy update.

findings.text: At 17:14 UTC checkout p95 increased (480ms→3180ms) and error rate rose (0.4%→7.4%) while request rate stayed ~115 rps; both old/new checkout cohorts degraded similarly.
Slow sampled traces show inventory spending most time in tcp.connect/handshake to inventory-db (~2450ms); 16/20 slow samples have DB handshakes >2000ms, while query and pool times are near baseline.

Scoped flow records from inventory subnet to inventory-db:5432 show rejected connections rising to 18% vs 0.1% baseline starting 17:14; a firewall policy update was applied to that path at 17:11, without request-level linkage yet.

Inventory-db CPU, successful SELECT p95, pool acquisition p95, and payment authorization p95 are near baseline; these measures cover successful operations and do not eliminate failed connection attempts or fully clear teams.

nextSteps: Network Platform should pull firewall-policy evaluation logs and rule-hit counters for the inventory-to-db path during 17:00–17:30, and compare rejects by source subnet, destination, and action (reject vs drop vs allow).

Inventory Services should correlate inventory-api connection-attempt failures/timeouts with the slow-trace timestamps and add per-attempt connect error/timeout metrics (including handshake duration) to validate whether rejects align with app-level failures.

Data Platform should verify inventory-db connection acceptance and auth logs (e.g., pg_hba/conf rejections vs max_connections saturation) for the window, and compare with the network reject timestamps to separate server-side rejects from network-policy rejects.
report.uncertainty: The evidence is consistent with a connectivity/policy issue on the inventory-to-db path, but there is no request-level linkage between flow rejects and the traced slow requests. Slow traces are sampled and don’t establish incident-wide prevalence.
report.customerUpdate: We’re seeing slower checkout requests and increased errors during the incident window. Traces suggest delays while connecting from the inventory service to its database, and network telemetry shows more rejected connections on that path. We’re validating whether a recent network policy change is related.

Checkout calls inventory then payments. Inventory reaches its database through the network path, which depends on the underlay. This catalog records dependencies, not causal propagation.
